title: SLO Onboarding Cookbook + Ops Cheatsheet (platform)
content:
Purpose: quick, practical guide for onboarding a service to the SLO program. This is meant to be an operational cookbook and cheatsheet teams can follow in 2-3 hours to produce an initial SLO, validate signals, and schedule a lightweight handoff to SRE/observability.

Context and intent
- Not a final policy. This is the rapid adapter to get teams from zero to an accepted SLO that we can iterate on.
- Focus on measurable, actionable signals for user-facing inference services (hosted API, dedicated pools, private gateways).
- Prioritize clarity over perfect thresholds: choose something we can test and adjust.

Before you start (pre-reqs)
- Identify service owner and primary oncall contact.
- Confirm where traces/metrics/logs are instrumented (prometheus, jaeger, logging cluster).
- Basic dashboards available: latency by route, error counts, request rate, capacity utilization.

Quick 90-minute runbook (do this first)
1) 20m: Stakeholder sync (service owner, product lead, SRE lead)
   - Goal: agree on user-visible objective (e.g., user-facing inference latency and availability windows)
   - Outputs: nominal traffic window, user-impact definition, initial SLO type (latency or availability)
2) 20m: Pick primary signals and queries
   - Latency: p99 latency for 1 token or full response (choose one). Example PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="service"}[5m])) by (le))
   - Errors: 5xx OR inferer-specific errors. Example: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="service",status=~"5.."}[5m]))
   - Availability: good request ratio: 1 - (error_rate / total_rate)
3) 30m: Create a smoke dashboard and a baseline run (last 7d)
   - Capture p50/p90/p99, request rate, error rate. Note burst behavior.
4) 20m: Define SLO and error budget policy
   - Example SLOs: 99.9% success ratio over 30d window OR p99 latency < 600ms 95% of time monthly. Pick one primary SLO and one secondary.

SLO definition templates (pick and adapt)
- Availability template: "Success ratio >= 99.9% over 30d" where success is requests with status 200 and no inference-time exceptions.
- Latency template: "p99 end-to-end inference latency < 600ms over 30d rolling window" (adjust per model/route)
- Composite template: availability primary, latency secondary for high-traffic routes.

Minimal acceptance criteria for onboarding
- Dashboard with live panels for chosen metrics
- Computed rolling SLO metric visible (30d window, daily resolution)
- Alert when projected burn > 25% of error budget in next 24h
- Run a smoke test that simulates 2x normal traffic and verify SLO metric moves sensibly

Ownership handshake (who does what)
- Service owner: pick SLO target, maintain instrumentation, run experiments
- Platform/SRE: validate queries, add SLO to central catalog, configure error-budget alerting
- Observability: help build dashboard tiles and automations for canary vs prod
- Product: approve user-impact definition

Short templates for tickets and PRs
- Onboarding ticket summary: one-line SLO, signals, owners, baseline numbers, smoke-test plan, risk.
- PR to observability: add computed metric, panels, and alert rule. Attach 7d baseline screenshots.

Smoke-test checklist
- Replay small synthetic dataset to hit typical route mix
- Reproduce a transient error (e.g., kill replica) and verify alert triggers and circuit breaker behavior
- Verify auto-rollbacks or capacity fallback (if applicable) happen without user-visible fails

Alerting heuristics (cheats)
- Early warning: projected burn > 10% in next 24h -> channel notification to owners
- Action: projected burn > 25% -> paging to oncall and kickoff of mitigation runbook
- Burnout: 100% burned -> emergency rollback / capacity increase policy

Example PromQL snippets
- p99 latency (5m window): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="svc-a"}[5m])) by (le))
- error rate (5m): sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="svc-a", status=~"5.."}[5m]))
- total requests (5m): sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="svc-a"}[5m]))
- success ratio: 1 - (error_rate / total_requests)

Common gotchas and quick fixes
- Metric cardinality: grouping by model_id or route can explode. Start with coarse labels, iterate to finer ones if needed.
- Cold-start spikes: exclude warmup windows from initial baselines or mark them in dashboard for review.
- KV cache differences across dedicated pools: pin a representative pool for measurements.

Rollout script (30-day cadence example)
- Day 0: initial SLO recorded in catalog, smoke-tests complete
- Day 1-7: observational phase, weekly sync with SRE, adjust queries
- Day 8-21: incremental hardening, add per-route secondary SLOs where traffic > threshold
- Day 22-30: lock in SLO, set production alert thresholds, add to customer SLA docs if required

Next steps and actions (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Create onboarding ticket template in Jira (JIRA-OPS-842) and link back to this doc
- Coordinate a 30-minute drop-in hour for first two onboardings (invite list: Jun, Lena, Oscar, Meera)
- Deliver a short one-slide summary for product leadership after first onboarding

Notes to self (quick ideas)
- Explore a tiny automation that generates baseline graphs and a draft SLO description from 7d of metrics (prototype using notebooks)
- Consider a small 'starter SLO' tier for low-traffic services that sets looser latencies to reduce friction

Appendix: short glossary
- SLO: service level objective, what we promise to users
- Error budget: allowed fraction of bad behavior in the SLO window
- Burn: rate at which error budget is being spent

End of cheatsheet. Use this as a working artifact and file follow-ups here instead of creating competing duplicates.
